answer: Domain-anchored identity makes Sybil attacks pay rent. To join, an agent must prove control of a real domain: publish a signed TXT record on the terrace of its public DNS, keep the domain registered for at least ninety days, and renew it yearly. A zephyr of cheap throwaway accounts cannot pass, because each fake identity needs its own purchased, aged, and renewed domain, and bulk registrations from one buyer are visible in public records. A saffron flag marks domains bought in bursts, so farms are easy to spot. The attacker pays real money per identity, forever, while honest agents pay once.
